name: issue_912_fan_only_runtime_not_reported_as_hvac
description: An occupant's overnight switch of the thermostat to fan_only (whole-house-fan-driven) is honoured as their override: no cool/heat is commanded while its grace runs, and the fan_only minutes are reported under their own runtime field, never blended into heat/cool runtime (Issue #912).
notes: Occupant impact: a Climate Advisor activity report told the occupant that heat or AC ran for
402 minutes overnight, when in fact only the whole-house fan / thermostat fan_only mode ran --
the compressor/burner never turned on. That's a false, alarming statement about energy use the
system never actually incurred.
Root cause (original design gap from Issue #114 / commit 95000bb, not a regression):
hvac_runtime_minutes on DailyRecord is meant to represent true compressor/burner runtime, but
the accumulation logic in coordinator.py was mode-agnostic -- it tracked ANY thermostat 'on'
state (including fan_only) via a single _hvac_on_since timer and flushed it into
hvac_runtime_minutes regardless of what mode was actually active.
Fix: fan_only sessions are now tracked under their own DailyRecord field
(thermostat_fan_only_runtime_minutes) via a dedicated _thermostat_fan_only_on_since timer, and
never start a thermal (compressor/burner) observation. A heat/cool<->fan_only transition with
no clean on/off edge (a common post-heat-cycle purge) is also handled via a new
_glide_hvac_session_mode() helper so the old mode's timer cannot silently keep accumulating
under the wrong field.
Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec 10), re-done for Issue #1297 (2026-11-03, owner-approved re-scope):
(a) Scenario effectiveness: the earlier note claimed the fan_only edges reached _async_thermostat_changed() and that
the harness could not observe the runtime split. Both were wrong. The scenario ran inside the harness's start-up
coalescing window, which never ended (Issue #1297), so _async_thermostat_changed() returned early for BOTH
thermostat changes and the old 'zero cool/heat commands until 04:45' assertion passed vacuously. And the real
end-of-day path does run here: thermal_learning_no_observations at 23:59 carries hvac_runtime_minutes and
thermostat_fan_only_runtime_minutes. The scenario is now steady-state (skip_startup_coalesce: true) and asserts
what production does: 22:05 fan_only is detected and confirmed as the occupant's override; no cool/heat is
commanded until its 15-minute grace ends at 22:20:30 (no set_temperature in (22:00:30, 22:20:29], and the plan's
first mode command at 22:20:30 still finds the thermostat in fan_only); the grace then ends and the plan resumes
(documented manual-override grace lifetime, docs/grace-periods-spec.md); the 15.5 fan_only minutes
(22:05:00-22:20:30) are reported as thermostat_fan_only_runtime_minutes; the 04:45 'off' is the occupant's
override. Verified by breaking it (Issue #1297 agent, test-only monkeypatches): with override detection disabled
the override assertions fail and CA re-commands cool at 22:05; with fan_only sessions counted as cool runtime
the runtime assertion fails.
The original '400 minutes with no commands' premise does not match production: a manual override's grace ends
after 15 minutes and the plan resumes.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: this scenario's premise (fan_only must never be tracked as
heat/cool runtime, and must never start a thermal observation) matches
docs/thermal-model-v3-spec.md's HVAC observation-type table and the DailyRecord field
documentation added alongside this fix.
(c) Occupant experience: after this fix, a fan-only-only night reports 0 min heat/cool runtime
with its fan-only minutes shown separately and correctly labeled -- never blended into a
number that implies the heater or AC ran, and never triggers a false 'thermal learning
found no observations despite N minutes of HVAC runtime' warning for a night when the
compressor/burner never engaged at all.

Issue #1310 (2026-11-03): the 23:59 thermal_learning_no_observations assertion is replaced by two field_equals checks on the day record production finalizes at 23:59 (engine_state._finalized_days, a passive harness copy of learning.record_day): thermostat_fan_only_runtime_minutes 15.5 and hvac_runtime_minutes 0.0. That watchdog only fires above 30 min of heat/cool runtime, and it fired here only because the harness thermostat kept reporting the stale 'fan' action after CA's 22:20:30 fan_only->cool (and had no hvac_action at all for the 22:00:30 cool), so production's mode fallback counted 103.5 min of AC runtime with the house at 70 F under a 72 F cool setpoint, where a real AC is idle. With the thermostat deriving its own action (#1310; config thermostat_reports_hvac_action seeds it from the first moment, as a thermostat that reports 'fan' at 22:05 always reports one) heat/cool runtime is 0 and the watchdog correctly stays silent -- the occupant outcome (c) below. The fan_only/heat-cool runtime split and the watchdog's silence are proven against the real coordinator by tests/test_hvac_session_detection.py; the #1310 thermostat by tests/test_fake_thermostat_action_1310.py.

Issue #1200 (2026-11-01): a whole-house fan install requires at least one door/window sensor; a sensorless WHF is unsupported. The scenario now configures binary_sensor.window, seeded closed at the first event (the real coordinator listener now sees its sensor events). Assertions unchanged; the event log gains sensor bookkeeping only.

events.note: Issue #1200: seeds the configured sensor closed so the coordinator reads a known state.

Warm evening, indoor already comfortably within the sleep comfort band (64-72F) -- the routine comfort-band arm has no reason to command cool or heat on its own. Cool outdoor air is available, favorable for a long whole-house-fan / thermostat fan_only run instead of running the compressor.
Normal evening classification: HVAC off recommended -- the compressor/burner is not expected to run at all tonight.

Thermostat (WHF-driven) enters fan_only mode. hvac_action reports 'fan' throughout this session -- never 'heating' or 'cooling' -- exactly the real-world signal pattern behind Issue #912's reported false runtime. This is the real _async_thermostat_changed turn-on edge: session_mode resolves to 'fan_only', _thermostat_fan_only_on_since is armed, and NO thermal (compressor/burner) observation starts.

Fan_only session ends after exactly 400 minutes (22:05 -> 04:45), matching Issue #912's reported ~402-minute magnitude. Compressor/burner never engaged at any point in this window. This is the real turn-off edge: thermostat_fan_only_runtime_minutes banks the full elapsed session, hvac_runtime_minutes is untouched, and _hvac_session_mode resets to None.

assertions.reason: Normal evening classification cycle runs as always.
The occupant switches the thermostat to fan_only at 22:05: production reads it as the occupant's change (not start-up noise, not CA's own echo).
After the 30 s confirm delay the fan_only override is confirmed and a manual grace (900 s) protects it.
While the occupant's fan_only override is protected, Climate Advisor writes no setpoint (every CA set_temperature bundles cool/heat, Issue #301).

Climate Advisor's first mode command after 22:05 comes when the grace ends, and it still finds the thermostat in fan_only: no cool/heat was commanded in between (a set_hvac_mode cool during the grace would make from_mode 'cool').
Production's documented override lifetime: the 15-minute manual grace ends and the plan resumes.
Issue #912: the day record production finalizes at 23:59 reports the 15.5 fan_only minutes (22:05:00-22:20:30) in their own field. Blended into heat/cool runtime this field would read 0.
Issue #912 / #1310: no heat/cool runtime on a night the compressor never ran -- not the fan_only minutes, and not CA's cool mode at 70 F under the 72 F ceiling (the AC is idle there).
The occupant's 04:45 'off' is seen as their own change.

verdict.summary: The occupant's overnight thermostat fan_only is honoured as their override (detected, confirmed, no cool/heat commanded during its grace), the plan resumes when the grace ends (Issue #912).
verdict.observed_behavior: 22:00 classification (cool armed at the sleep ceiling 72) -> 22:05 occupant sets fan_only: override_detected, whole-house-fan reconcile turns fan.whf off (no cool/heat) -> 22:05:30 override_confirmed, grace 900 s -> no setpoint/mode command until 22:20:30 -> grace expires, plan resumes cool (thermostat_mode_set fan_only->cool) -> the AC stays idle (house 70 F under the 72 F ceiling), so no heat/cool runtime and no 23:59 runtime watchdog -> 04:45 occupant 'off' detected as override.
verdict.expected_behavior: The occupant's activity report shows 0 minutes of heat/cool runtime and the fan-only runtime separately and correctly labeled for this night -- never a false claim that the heater or AC ran, and never a false 'thermal learning found no observations' warning for a night when the compressor/burner never engaged at all. This scenario proves the fan_only session-tracking code path is command-inert; the numeric DailyRecord split and the watchdog's silence are proven directly against the real coordinator by tests/test_hvac_session_detection.py and tests/test_coordinator.py (see note (a)).
